subject: Quarterline: weekly exec readout — wins, near-term risks, asks
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: QBR Consultants <qbr-consultant@strategyfirm.com>
Date: 2026-12-21T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Quarterline: weekly exec readout — wins, near-term risks, asks

Team — attaching this week's concise readout as we lock the QBR pack. Short version up top, details below. Please scan and flag anything that should move higher on the agenda.

Wins:
- Slate of infra optimizations (batching + KV cache) reduced avg token cost ~14% on staging for long-doc generation; validated on 2 representative customer prompts.
- Successful dry-run with Acme integration team: latency SLOs hold under 75th percentile load.
- New quantization profile rolled into canary (int8-mix) with no observable quality regressions on our eval set.

Near-term risks:
- Capacity: Dedicated fleet rebalancing scheduled 01/04 may cause short 30–60m throttling windows if fallback policies aren't exercised. Need a canary and rollback plan.
- QBR slides currently missing clear cost delta table for model mix recommendation (hosted vs dedicated).
- One outstanding security question from Acme re: audit log retention (they requested 7 years).

Asks (action owners / ETA):
- Jonas: provide a 1-pager canary/rollback runbook and estimate of expected throttling exposure by 12/23. (Attachment: canary-plan.docx)
- Marcus: update cost delta table for the three model families and add a short note on expected unit economics by 12/27.
- Laura: prioritize the audit-log ask; want proposed language we can present to Acme on 12/24.
- All: review QBR_Pack_Draft_v1.pdf in the Drive link below and add comments by EOD 12/24.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QBR-Quarterline-Pack
Attachments: QBR_Pack_Draft_v1.pdf

Thanks — will incorporate items into the final deck after comments.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-21T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quarterline: weekly exec readout — wins, near-term risks, asks

Vanessa — thanks for the crisp readout. Quick notes inline.

> Near-term risks:
> - Capacity: Dedicated fleet rebalancing scheduled 01/04 may cause short 30–60m throttling windows if fallback policies aren't exercised. Need a canary and rollback plan.

Can you quantify expected error/retry rates we should bake into the canary? If the throttling window is 30–60m and we lose 10–15% throughput, what is the customer impact in terms of requests/min? I'd like a concise table for the QBR.

> Asks (action owners / ETA):
> - Marcus: update cost delta table for the three model families and add a short note on expected unit economics by 12/27.

Make sure the cost table highlights two alternatives: short-term (quantization + caching) vs medium-term (model pruning + dedicated commit). The execs will want clear dollars saved per million tokens.

Laura
VP, Engineering Operations

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-12-22T08:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quarterline: weekly exec readout — wins, near-term risks, asks

Adding the canary context here. I've attached the initial canary-plan.docx. TL;DR:
- Canary window: 01/03 02:00–06:00 UTC (warm-up + progressive traffic ramp).
- Expected temporary throughput drop: up to ~12% during peak roll step; we will route priority routes to fallback model variants during the 15m progressive step to keep p95 under SLO when possible.
- Rollback thresholds: 5% increase in error-rate OR 20% CPU utilization delta sustained > 10m.

I'll put the expected customer impact table into the Drive doc and add a small simulation for the 3 largest customers (Acme, BrightLane, NovaRetail) so the QBR can reference concrete numbers.

Attachment: canary-plan.docx

— Jonas
Senior Director, Reliability

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: QBR Consultants <qbr-consultant@strategyfirm.com>
Date: 2026-12-24T10:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quarterline: weekly exec readout — wins, near-term risks, asks

Thanks — Jonas and Laura, this is helpful. I updated the deck in Drive (qbr_slide_deck_v2.pptx) and added a short appendix with the simulated customer impact table Jonas mentioned. Summary of changes and next steps: 

What I changed:
- Added cost delta table (Marcus, please verify the unit numbers) and a 1-slide summary of recommended model mix.
- Inserted canary runbook summary and rollback thresholds in the operational appendix.
- Drafted proposed language for audit-log retention and a suggested customer-facing note (see slide A3).

Open items / requests:
- Marcus: please drop the final numbers into the cost table by 12/27. I'll call out the table on the QBR agenda and ask you to speak to it.
- Laura: can you confirm the audit retention phrasing by 12/24 EOD so we can close the Acme thread?
- All: small request to the leadership distro — can we schedule a 30-minute pre-QBR rehearsal (see proposed slot below)?

Proposed rehearsal slot: 2027-01-04 09:00–09:30 PT (calendar invite attached: pre-qbr-dryrun-20270104.ics)
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QBR-Quarterline-Pack
Attachments: qbr_slide_deck_v2.pptx, pre-qbr-dryrun-20270104.ics

— Vanessa
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-12-28T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quarterline: weekly exec readout — wins, near-term risks, asks

All — reviewed the updated deck and appendix. I've added the finalized cost deltas and a short note on sensitivity assumptions (attachment added to Drive). Two quick items:

1) The numbers assume the int8-mix profile at 0.92 quality multiplier; if QA flags anything on the eval prompts we should switch the table to the conservative row.
2) I’m good with the rehearsal slot on 01/04; Vanessa please send the calendar invite to the leadership distro and include the 15-minute tech-check window before the rehearsal.

Approved from my side for the QBR pack pending Laura's audit-language sign-off.

Attachment: pre-qbr-dryrun-20270104.ics (calendar invite)

— Marcus Lin
Director, Product Strategy
Redwood Inference
